Real SEO work requested by the owner: they want the ~45,761 NxLabs mod detail pages (and growing) to be genuinely discoverable, and want better on-page SEO for them generally. IMPORTANT: another agent is concurrently finishing a real backfill (`scripts/backfill-upstream-updated.ts`, adding `GameMod.upstreamUpdatedAt`) and has uncommitted changes in `app/(marketing)/mods/games/[family]/page.tsx`, `app/(marketing)/mods/page.tsx`, `components/mods/ModCard.tsx`, `lib/mods-catalog.ts`, `prisma/schema.prisma`. Before touching ANY of those files, run `git status` and `git diff` to see the current state — if that agent has since committed, `git pull` first. If it's still uncommitted when you need to touch one of those files, read the actual current on-disk content (not what you'd expect from git history) and make your edit additive to what's already there, the same careful merge behavior other agents used tonight to avoid clobbering concurrent work. ## Problem 1 — sitemap capacity (the actual discoverability blocker) `app/sitemap.ts` returns ONE flat array combining all static marketing routes + all mod detail URLs (via `listCatalogSlugs()` from `lib/mods-catalog.ts`) — confirmed live moments ago at 45,761 mod URLs + ~1,460 other pages ≈ 47,000+ combined. Google's sitemap protocol hard-caps a single sitemap file at 50,000 URLs (and 50MB uncompressed). This will breach that ceiling on the next import. Fix: implement a real sitemap INDEX using Next.js App Router's `generateSitemaps()` API (read the Next.js docs/existing examples if unfamiliar — this generates multiple `/sitemap/[id].xml`-style files under one index automatically). Split mod URLs into chunks safely under 50,000 each (e.g. one sitemap per ~10,000-20,000 URLs, leaving real headroom, not cutting it close), keep the existing static marketing routes on their own dedicated sitemap (id 0), and mod pages chunked across the rest. Read `app/sitemap.ts` in full first — preserve every existing static route entry exactly as-is, only restructure HOW they're chunked/served, not what's included. Verify locally (or against a running dev/staging instance if idle) that `/sitemap.xml` (the index) and the sub-sitemaps actually resolve and contain valid, non-overlapping, complete URL sets — total count across all sub-sitemaps must still equal the real total (do the math, don't just eyeball it). ## Problem 2 — on-page SEO quality for mod detail pages Read `app/(marketing)/mods/[family]/[slug]/page.tsx`'s current `generateMetadata` in full first. Real, concrete improvements: 1. **Meta description quality**: if the current meta description just uses the short `description` (often thin/one-line, sometimes literally missing pre-backfill), improve it to prefer the real `longDescription` field (added tonight, backfilled from Modrinth's real project body) when available, trimmed to a proper meta-description length (~150-160 chars), falling back to the short description, never fabricating text that isn't real. 2. **Structured data (JSON-LD)**: add real `schema.org` markup — `SoftwareApplication` is the closest fit for a mod/plugin. Populate ONLY real fields: `name`, `description`, `applicationCategory`, `image` (real iconUrl/gallery), `datePublished`/`dateModified` (use real `createdAt`/`upstreamUpdatedAt` when present, omit `dateModified` entirely if `upstreamUpdatedAt` is null rather than guessing), `aggregateRating` (ONLY when `ratingCount > 0` using the real `avgRating`/`ratingCount` — omit the whole property when there are zero ratings, never fabricate a rating), `author` (real `authorName` when present). Never include a field you don't have real data for. 3. **Open Graph / Twitter card tags**: real per-mod `og:image` (the mod's real icon or first gallery image), `og:title`, `og:description` — check if `generateMetadata`'s return already includes an `openGraph`/`twitter` block; if not, add one using real data only. 4. **Image alt text**: `components/mods/ModCard.tsx` currently renders `` — empty alt on a genuinely content-bearing image (the mod's own icon, not decorative) is a real accessibility/SEO gap. Change to a real descriptive alt (e.g. `${mod.name} icon`) on the CARD's icon image specifically (not on any genuinely decorative background art elsewhere — use judgment on which images are content vs. decoration). 5. **Canonical URL**: check whether the marketing (`/mods/[family]/[slug]`) and portal (`/dashboard/nxlabs/[family]/[slug]`) pages could read as duplicate content to a crawler (the portal one probably isn't indexed at all since `/dashboard` is disallowed in `robots.txt` — verify this is actually true and sufficient, rather than assuming; if the portal page IS somehow crawlable, add an explicit canonical pointing at the marketing URL). ## CRITICAL process rule (still in force from tonight's incident) Multiple agents running their own `deploy-staging.sh`/`promote-production.sh` concurrently corrupted the build output earlier tonight and caused a real production outage. **Do NOT run `deploy-staging.sh` or `promote-production.sh` yourself.** Before starting, run `ps aux | grep -E "next build|deploy-staging|promote-production"` — if anything is running, poll every 30s until clear. Make your changes, verify with `npx tsc --noEmit`, commit and push to `main`, then STOP. I (the parent session) am batching commits and will deploy everything together myself. ## Process (mandatory) - Read `app/sitemap.ts`, `app/(marketing)/mods/[family]/[slug]/page.tsx`, `lib/mods-catalog.ts`, `components/mods/ModCard.tsx`, and `app/robots.ts` in full before editing. - DB reads only via `db` from `lib/db`. Never print a raw psql/DATABASE_URL string. - `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. - Commit and push to `main` (check `git log origin/main` before/after for concurrent pushes — coordinate/re-pull rather than force-push if origin moved). Report back: confirmation the sitemap index correctly covers the full real URL count with no page exceeding 50,000 (show the actual chunk math), and a summary of exactly which real fields you populated in the structured data / meta tags (and which you correctly omitted for lack of real data).

### Generating multiple sitemaps

While a single sitemap will work for most applications. For large web applications, you may need to split a sitemap into multiple files.

There are two ways you can create multiple sitemaps:

* By nesting `sitemap.(xml|js|ts)` inside multiple route segments e.g. `app/sitemap.xml` and `app/products/sitemap.xml`.
* By using the [`generateSitemaps`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-sitemaps) function.

For example, to split a sitemap using `generateSitemaps`, return an array of objects with the sitemap `id`. Then, use the `id` to generate the unique sitemaps.

```ts filename="app/product/sitemap.ts" switcher
import type { MetadataRoute } from 'next'
import { BASE_URL } from '@/app/lib/constants'

export async function generateSitemaps() {
  // Fetch the total number of products and calculate the number of sitemaps needed
  return [{ id: 0 }, { id: 1 }, { id: 2 }, { id: 3 }]
}

export default async function sitemap(props: {
  id: Promise<string>
}): Promise<MetadataRoute.Sitemap> {
  const id = await props.id
  // Google's limit is 50,000 URLs per sitemap
  const start = id * 50000
  const end = start + 50000
  const products = await getProducts(
    `SELECT id, date FROM products WHERE id BETWEEN ${start} AND ${end}`
  )
  return products.map((product) => ({
    url: `${BASE_URL}/product/${product.id}`,
    lastModified: product.date,
  }))
}
```

export async function generateSitemaps() {

  return [{ id: 0 }, { id: 1 }, { id: 2 }, { id: 3 }]
}

export default async function sitemap(props) {
  const id = await props.id
  // Google's limit is 50,000 URLs per sitemap
  const start = id * 50000
  const end = start + 50000

input.title: Fix pingIndexNow's 10k-URL cap for full catalogue resubmit
input.tldr: While fixing the NxLabs sitemap (splitting 45,761 mod URLs into chunked sitemaps), I found lib/indexnow.ts's submitSitemapToIndexNow() claims to submit "every URL" but pingIndexNow silently caps at 10,000 per call — so a bulk resubmit after a big catalogue change would report submitting ~47,000 URLs while actually only pinging the first 10,000. Worth batching pingIndexNow into multiple calls (or documenting the real behavior) so the reported count matches what's actually submitted.
input.prompt:
In /opt/nxeon, lib/indexnow.ts has pingIndexNow(urls) which silently does `.slice(0, 10000)` before submitting to the IndexNow API — a real, undocumented-to-callers cap. submitSitemapToIndexNow() (same file) is meant to submit EVERY URL in the sitemap for a one-off bulk resubmit, and returns `{ submitted: urls.length }` as if the full count were pinged, but internally only the first 10,000 of whatever it passes to pingIndexNow actually reach the API — the rest are silently dropped, and the returned count is misleading (it reports the full url count, not what was actually sent).

This was already true before tonight's sitemap-chunking work, but is more likely to matter now that app/sitemap.ts's mod catalogue alone is 45,761+ URLs (see app/sitemap.ts and lib/sitemap-mods.ts, restructured tonight into a chunked sitemap index for Google's 50k-URL-per-file cap).

Fix: either (a) make pingIndexNow batch through the full url list in chunks of 10,000 (looping calls to the IndexNow API) so a full-catalogue resubmit actually reaches the API, or (b) at minimum make submitSitemapToIndexNow's returned `submitted` count reflect what was actually pinged, not the full candidate list, so callers aren't misled. Read both functions in lib/indexnow.ts in full before changing anything — pingIndexNow is also called elsewhere for single/small URL lists (e.g. after a blog publish), so keep that call path's behavior identical for small inputs.
